verified_against_commit: 2959d7a (full codebase reviewed by mentor before spec authoring; all file paths, line references, field names, and patterns below are verified facts, not guesses)

rules: Author and edit files only. Do NOT execute git commands, AWS CLI commands, docker commands, npm installs, or deployments.
Do NOT self-approve or mark tasks complete. Report changed file paths; the human runs all verification gates and commands.
If actual code differs from what this spec states (line numbers may drift slightly), STOP and report the discrepancy before editing. Do not silently adapt.

New files use LF line endings. Do NOT mass-convert line endings of existing files (ActivityForm.js currently has CRLF; edit it in place without converting untouched lines' endings if the editor allows, and do not let a save rewrite the whole file's endings silently).
Never write credentials, connection strings, account IDs, or secrets into any file.
Do not modify any file outside each task's files_in_scope.
Do not add npm dependencies, Python packages, or AWS resources. Everything below uses only what exists.
Aesthetics rule: introduce ZERO new visual styles. Every new UI element must reuse an existing CSS class or component pattern named in its task. No new colors, fonts, spacings, or button shapes.

context.app: Cruddur microblogging app. Flask backend (gunicorn) + React (react-router v6, createBrowserRouter) frontend. RDS PostgreSQL for users/activities, DynamoDB for DMs. Avatars served from https://assets.fentoncruddur.com/avatars/processed/{cognito_user_id}.jpg via ProfileAvatar component.
context.auth_pattern: JWT verification exists and works. Reference implementation: data_update_profile in backend-flask/app.py (~line 505): extract_access_token(request.headers) -> cognito_jwt_token.verify(access_token) -> claims['sub'] is the cognito_user_id -> TokenVerifyError except-branch returns {}, 401. Frontend token pattern: getAccessToken() from components/lib/CheckAuth.js, sent as 'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}` (see UserFeedPage.js loadData).
context.signed_in_user_object: checkAuth(setUser) in components/lib/CheckAuth.js sets user = { display_name, handle, cognito_user_id } from Cognito attributes. Pages hold it in `user` state and pass it to DesktopNavigation/DesktopSidebar as props.user.
context.profile_route: /@:handle -> UserFeedPage (verified in App.js). New-message route: /messages/new/:handle -> MessageGroupNewPage (verified in App.js).
context.goal: Make the app multi-user-correct and self-discoverable for a 10-30 person closed beta.

tasks.title: P0 - Real post attribution: replace hardcoded user_handle with JWT identity (backend + frontend)
tasks.why: backend-flask/app.py line ~446 hardcodes user_handle = 'chrisfenton' in data_activities. Every user's post is attributed to chrisfenton. ActivityForm.js also sends no Authorization header, so identity cannot currently reach the backend.

changes.instruction: Import getAccessToken from '../components/lib/CheckAuth' (adjust relative path: this file lives in components/, so './lib/CheckAuth'). In onsubmit, before the fetch, call const accessToken = await getAccessToken(); and add 'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}` to the headers object, exactly mirroring the header pattern in UserFeedPage.js loadData.

Replace the hardcoded user_handle = 'chrisfenton' with the exact auth pattern from data_update_profile in this same file: access_token = extract_access_token(request.headers); claims = cognito_jwt_token.verify(access_token); cognito_user_id = claims['sub']; wrapped so TokenVerifyError returns {}, 401. Pass cognito_user_id (NOT a handle) to CreateActivity.run. Keep the existing OPTIONS preflight handling and debug logging structure.

Change run(message, user_handle, ttl) to run(message, cognito_user_id, ttl). Update the validation branch from user_handle checks to cognito_user_id checks (error key 'cognito_user_id_blank'). Pass cognito_user_id through create_activity() into the SQL params as 'cognito_user_id'. Do not change the TTL logic, response model shape, or query_object_activity.

Change the inner SELECT's WHERE clause from users.handle = %(handle)s to users.cognito_user_id = %(cognito_user_id)s. This mirrors the existing lookup in db/sql/activities/users/uuid_from_cognito_user_id.sql. Nothing else in the file changes.

tasks.explicitly_not_in_scope: data_activities_reply (~line 481) has the same hardcoded handle, but CreateReply is a non-persisting mock (writes nothing to the database). Fixing replies requires a schema migration (reply_to_activity_uuid is typed integer but must hold a UUID) and is deferred to a separate spec by human decision. Do not touch reply code in this spec.

tasks.title: P1 - Avatar + counts on new posts: response shape parity in object.sql
tasks.why: ActivityForm prepends the create-response object directly into the feed (setActivities(current => [data,...current])). The feed's ProfileAvatar reads activity.cognito_user_id and ActivityItem reads replies_count/reposts_count/likes_count. home.sql returns all of these; object.sql returns none of them, so a fresh post renders a broken avatar and empty counts until refresh.

changes.instruction: Add these five fields to the SELECT so its output shape matches home.sql exactly for all fields the frontend consumes: users.cognito_user_id, activities.replies_count, activities.reposts_count, activities.likes_count, activities.reply_to_activity_uuid. Keep existing fields and the INNER JOIN/WHERE unchanged.

tasks.title: P1 - Fix hardcoded Profile nav link
tasks.why: DesktopNavigation.js line ~28 hardcodes url="/@chrisfenton" for the Profile link. Every user's Profile button navigates to chrisfenton's page.

changes.instruction: In the props.user branch, change the profileLink url to a template using the signed-in user's handle: url={"/@" + props.user.handle}. The user object is guaranteed to have .handle here (set by checkAuth). No other nav items change in this task.

tasks.title: P2 - Profile page: Edit Profile for self, Message button for others
tasks.why: ProfileHeading.js renders EditProfileButton unconditionally, including on other users' profiles. For beta discovery, viewing someone else's profile should offer Message instead, linking into the existing /messages/new/:handle flow.

changes.instruction: Pass the signed-in user into the heading: <ProfileHeading setPopped={setPoppedProfile} profile={profile} user={user} />. No other changes to this page.

Compute const isOwnProfile = props.user && props.profile && props.user.handle === props.profile.handle. Render EditProfileButton only when isOwnProfile. When not own profile (and props.profile.handle exists), render a react-router <Link to={'/messages/new/' + props.profile.handle} className='profile_edit_btn'>Message</Link> in the exact same position in the .info div where EditProfileButton sits. Import Link from react-router-dom.
changes.aesthetics: Reuse the existing .profile_edit_btn class from EditProfileButton.css verbatim (pill border, transparent background, hover fill). Do not create a new CSS class or file. The Message link occupies the same slot as Edit Profile, so layout is unchanged. Note: .profile_edit_btn styles a <button>; applied to a <Link> (renders <a>), add ONLY text-decoration: none via the existing class if links show underline - if needed, extend EditProfileButton.css with a.profile_edit_btn { text-decoration: none; } and nothing else.

tasks.title: P2 - Make sidebar SuggestedUserItem clickable
tasks.why: ActivityContent already links usernames to /@handle (verified). The only user-rendering component with no link is SuggestedUserItem.js.

changes.instruction: Import Link from react-router-dom and wrap the existing .user div's contents in (or convert the outer div to) a <Link to={'/@' + props.handle}> preserving the existing className='user' on the rendered element so SuggestedUserItem.css applies unchanged. Add no new styles beyond text-decoration handling if underlines appear (match the approach used in Task D).

tasks.title: P2 - People directory: backend endpoint + /people page + nav link
tasks.why: There is no way to discover users you haven't seen post. A flat directory closes the loop for beta scale.

changes.instruction: SELECT users.uuid, users.handle, users.display_name, users.cognito_user_id FROM public.users ORDER BY users.display_name ASC. Return all rows as a JSON array using the same COALESCE(array_to_json(array_agg(row_to_json(...)))) wrapping pattern found in db/sql/users/show.sql's activities subquery, so db.query_array_json (or the array-json helper used elsewhere in lib/db.py - check which helper home_activities.py uses and match it) returns a clean array.

Mirror users_short.py exactly in structure: from lib.db import db; class UsersIndex with run() (no args); sql = db.template('users','index'); return the query result. Use the array-returning query helper consistent with how home_activities.py returns its list.

Register @app.route("/api/users", methods=['GET','OPTIONS']) with @cross_origin(), following the decorator style of data_messages (~line 271). Handler: import UsersIndex alongside the existing service imports, return UsersIndex.run(), 200. Handle OPTIONS with the same early-return pattern used in data_activities. IMPORTANT: use the path /api/users, NOT /api/users/@all, to avoid any ambiguity with the existing /api/users/@<string:handle>/short route.

Mirror the structure of NotificationsFeedPage.js (simplest existing authenticated page): imports DesktopNavigation and DesktopSidebar, checkAuth(setUser) + dataFetchedRef pattern in useEffect, loadData fetching `${process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/api/users` with the Authorization Bearer header via getAccessToken. Render inside the standard <article> / DesktopNavigation / <div className='content'> / DesktopSidebar skeleton. In the content area render a heading 'People' styled like other pages' headers (copy the title markup/classes used in NotificationsFeedPage or MessageGroupsPage), then one row per user: ProfileAvatar (id={user.cognito_user_id}) + display_name + @handle, the whole row wrapped in <Link to={'/@' + user.handle}>.
changes.aesthetics: Row markup and class names must copy SuggestedUserItem's structure (.user / .identity / .display_name / .handle) and PeoplePage.css should import/duplicate only those existing rules from SuggestedUserItem.css - no new visual language. Rows are a vertical list in the main content column, same width behavior as the activity feed. No cards, no grids, no new colors.

changes.instruction: Add route { path: "/people", element: <PeoplePage /> } to createBrowserRouter, placed after /notifications. Import PeoplePage with the other page imports.

Inside the props.user branch, add a peopleLink DesktopNavigationLink with url="/people", name="People", handle="people", active={props.active}, rendered between messagesLink and profileLink. First read DesktopNavigationLink.js to see how it maps `handle` to an icon; if it has a fixed icon mapping with no entry for 'people', reuse the closest existing icon mapping mechanism rather than adding a new svg - report what you find in the completion report. Set active={'people'} on PeoplePage's DesktopNavigation usage.

post_deploy_human_tests: TWO-ACCOUNT ATTRIBUTION TEST (the decisive one): sign in as a second test account, post a crud, confirm it appears under that account's name and avatar - not chrisfenton. This proves Task A end to end.
Fresh-post rendering: post a crud and confirm avatar AND action counts render immediately without refresh (Task B).
Profile nav: as the second account, click Profile in the nav - it must land on that account's own page (Task C).
Discovery loop: home feed -> tap a username -> profile shows Message button (not Edit Profile) -> tap Message -> compose view at /messages/new/:handle (Task D).
Own profile still shows Edit Profile and it still opens the profile form (Task D regression check).
Sidebar suggested user navigates to their profile (Task E).
People page: /people lists all seeded users with avatars, each row navigates to the right profile; People nav item highlights when active (Task F).
DM regression: send a DM through the existing flow to confirm nothing in the message pages broke.
deploy_notes_for_human: Frontend changes require a full React image rebuild and push (REACT_APP_* vars bake at build time); capture the new sha256 digest and pin it in config.toml per the established ECR digest-pinning practice.
Backend changes require backend image rebuild + digest pin likewise.
First deploy session should also: rotate the C.Fenton_CLI access key (scheduled item) and re-enable the CodePipeline Build inbound transition.
